The other free image models cost the same or more, so trying them would fail the same way. Once you add credits or your balance refreshes, I can run the same request again.

**Here's the request I'd send:**
> Professional product photo of one clean white leather sneaker, angled three-quarter side view, centred on a plain white background, soft even studio lighting, a faint natural shadow under the shoe, sharp focus on the leather and stitching, nothing else in the frame (no text, logos or props).

**About your worry over whether the photo will look right:** a shot like that fits most marketplace rules for a main image.
- **Plain white background:** many marketplaces require this.
- **Just the product:** many marketplaces also require this.
- **Square:** shows up well in search results.
- **Three-quarter angle:** shows both the side and the toe, which is how buyers usually judge sneakers.

One thing to keep in mind: an AI-generated image shows *a* white sneaker, not your exact pair. Many marketplaces want photos of the actual item, especially for used shoes. If you have a photo of your own shoe, attach it once you have credits. I can remove the background and put it on clean white for 5 credits. That's usually the safer choice for a listing.
